newsitem.title: INDIA: India's HZL plans smelter, power plant.
newsitem.headline: India's HZL plans smelter, power plant.

text.p: India's state-owned Hindustan Zinc Ltd (HZL) plans to set up a 60,000-tonnes-per-year green field zinc smelter, a Mines Ministry statement said on Thursday.

The statement said a proposal for setting up the smelter, at an estimated cost of six billion rupees ($167 million), has been submitted for approval to a sub-committee of the government's Public Investment Board.
HZL has also decided to set up a 100-megawatt power plant at an estimated cost of four billion rupees in a joint venture, the statement said.
It did not say where the two projects would be located or give details on when the power plant would be built or the joint venture partner or partners.

The company is expected to expand its Rampura Agucha zinc-lead mine in western Rajasthan state to an annual capacity of 1.35 million tonnes from the present 900,000 tonnes by the end of the year, it said.
The statement said the company estimated lead-zinc concentrates output for 1996/97 (April-March) at 340,000 tonnes and lead-zinc metal output for the year at 143,000 tonnes.
It did not give production figures for 1995/96.
The company has projected lead-zinc concentrates output in 1997/98 at 343,500 tonnes and lead-zinc metal at 168,500 tonnes.
